summary: This program stores four song titles in a PriorityQueue and then removes them one at a time, showing that a priority queue hands back its smallest element first — here, the title that comes first alphabetically.

lines.code: PriorityQueue<String> titleQueue = new PriorityQueue<>(); // natural A–Z order
lines.text: A PriorityQueue keeps its elements ordered by priority rather than by arrival. With no comparator supplied, Strings use their natural order, so the alphabetically first title has the highest priority.
The offer method adds an element to the queue; the queue itself decides where it belongs internally, so the insertion order does not matter.
Iterating a PriorityQueue does not walk the elements in sorted order — only the head is guaranteed to be the smallest, which is why the printout looks partly shuffled.
Looping until the queue is empty drains it completely, one element per pass.

lines.code: String nextTitle = titleQueue.poll(); // removes smallest (A–Z) first
lines.text: The poll method removes and returns the head of the queue, so repeated calls deliver the titles in full alphabetical order: Circle of Life, Clair de Lune, One More Time, Respect.
